chapter: Second European tour and the crash
title: Touring Europe on short engagements and the second Barcelona visit
summary: Wooding took whole seasons when places could pay, but mostly stayed under a month, with three months at Haus Germania in Berlin.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay, so you went all over Europe again.
And all through the rest of 1927. Do you remember what month you went over in '27?
Was it late in the year?
It was one of the warm months, I don't remember exactly now, but it was one of the warm months, because we didn't wear any overcoats, you see.
I see. So what happened. You went all over, I guess through 1928 and 1929. And I know, in 1929, at one point, you were in Barcelona and you made some records.
That was the second time we'd been in Barcelona.
Right. And you made records in Barcelona that time.
And this time I guess you were --
You see, now we were playing a lot of times not just for a week or one concert, but whenever I could get --
Get a whole season, right? A season.
Didn't you play whole seasons in places?
No, we very seldom stayed over a month. Except on place in the Haus GERMANIA, which was in Scharlotten-burg in Berlin. We played three months.

Because, in order to take up the time now we were on our own. And we didn't, but some places like Holland and Belgium -- we stayed something like fifteen days in Belgium. But some of the places couldn't afford to pay a band like that. So when we got to a place that could afford to pay, we squeezed it as long as we could.
